name: Jeremy Corbyn
role: Leader of the UK Labour Party
description: British Labour leader who advocated public ownership, stronger welfare provision and less military intervention.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Elections, parliamentary scrutiny and a public Brexit vote were central to his political programme.
axes.counter: Specific recall mechanisms and expert-government hypotheticals are analogical estimates.

axes.brief: Civil liberties, peaceful protest and opposition to surveillance framed his programme.
axes.counter: Public safety and regulated firearms still justified state restrictions.

axes.brief: His programme supported multicultural recognition, Indigenous rights and minority protection.
axes.counter: Pluralism did not entail eliminating all shared civic requirements.

axes.brief: Migrant rights, family unity and refugee protection were supported.
axes.counter: Labour’s negotiated migration system was not an unlimited right of settlement.

axes.brief: Corbyn opposed Iraq and nuclear deterrence and prioritised conflict prevention.
axes.counter: Labour’s 2019 manifesto retained NATO and Trident commitments he personally disputed.

axes.brief: International solidarity and human-rights cooperation coexisted with longstanding EU scepticism.
axes.counter: The leadership period includes support for Remain and a negotiated Brexit referendum.

axes.brief: Utilities, rail, mail and broadband were proposed for public ownership.
axes.counter: The manifesto did not nationalise every private company or all routine contracting.

axes.brief: Trade was to protect labour standards and domestic capacity alongside international cooperation.
axes.counter: Worker protections are not evidence for every tariff or strategic ownership restriction.

axes.brief: Industrial strategy, wage floors and public investment accompanied continued private enterprise.
axes.counter: Consumer-led production and entrepreneurship remained legitimate.

axes.brief: His programme proposed substantial tax-funded redistribution and stronger income support.
axes.counter: Precise mechanisms such as compulsory compensated land redistribution remain inferred.

axes.brief: Civil law, religious freedom and opposition to religious discrimination framed his position.
axes.counter: State ceremonies and holidays are not equivalent to clergy control of legislation.

axes.brief: Equal treatment of LGBT people, gender equality and reproductive choice were supported.
axes.counter: All specific school and language policies are not individually documented.

axes.brief: Green industrial development and housing investment coexisted with environmental precaution.
axes.counter: Opposition to ecological harm does not entail opposition to all technical progress.

axes.brief: Regional empowerment and community ownership accompanied nationwide welfare standards.
axes.counter: Local participation does not imply unrestricted secession or local tax retention.

axes.brief: His explanations of inequality emphasised discrimination, education and social conditions.
axes.counter: Specific comparative genetic explanations remain weakly evidenced.
axes.gap: These are provisional causal estimates from social-equality explanations; support for equality alone cannot prove a biological or social theory.
